items.title: aggregator(forecast): one forecast contract for Roadmap and Projects (#3984)
items.body: Implements #3984 (design `doc/2026-11-01T21-07-00Z_design_pm-stack_forecasting.md` §4, parent chain #1184 → #1256): one machine-first forecast contract that Roadmap and Projects consume identically. ## What lands - **`src/forecast-contract.ts`** — the shared contract (`forecast-contract/v1`). Three separate forecast types, so missing data in one plane never makes another look more certain: - `epic_completion` — wraps `deriveEpicEta` (#3982): scope/subject, `asOf`, model version, input window/coverage, remaining units, nullable P50/P80, confidence (evidence grade), baseline source, structured `reasons`/`limitations`. GitHub-vs-Project status disagreement is surfaced as a structured reason, never resolved silently. - `quota_exhaustion` — per-pool wall interval from a measured burn rate in the pool's own units, with next reset, remaining/limit, and before/after-reset disposition. The per-pool rate-history model is #3983 (still open); absent/stale/zero rate ⇒ the first-class `quota_rate_unavailable` / `no_recent_burn` states — no invented date, never "safe". A single linear rate collapses the interval to the point estimate and says so in `limitations`. - `stall_risk` — wraps `deriveStallRisk` (§3): score + threshold + contributing signals; unknown signals are named limitations; `escalatesToNeedsYou` stays `false`. - `formatForecastSummary` — the one-line rendering both pages share: range (or named no-date state) + confidence + input summary together. Never a bare date; missing values never render as zero. - **`GET /api/forecasts.json`** — serves the identical contract objects (`?subject=` filters). Epic/stall subjects derive from the stored item history (#3981, new `cfg.itemHistoryFile` / `PM_AGG_ITEM_HISTORY_FILE`, default state-dir `item-history.jsonl`); quota contracts build from the live quota view (token burn rate only when the window unit is tokens and gatherer freshness is ok). - **Rendering** — Roadmap drill-down (matched epic) and Projects pool cards render the same summaries via optional `forecasts` maps threaded through `renderRoadmap` / `projectsBodyHtml` / `renderProgram`; absent forecasts render exactly as before. ## Tests `test/forecast-contract-3984.test.ts` (16 tests, named oracle = design §4): high/low (borrowed baseline)/unavailable confidence, stale source, missing baseline/limit/reset, all three forecast types, plus Roadmap + Projects rendering of the same contract. Full aggregator suite: 1830 pass / 18 fail — identical 18 failures on a clean-main baseline worktree (1814 pass / 18 fail), so no regressions; `tsc --noEmit` clean on touched files. Queue: task 14323 (replacement for task 12141), lane code-k, execution lane direct. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: feat(aggregator): forecast backtest + calibration report (#3986)
items.body: Closes #3986. ## What lands Forecasts (ETA bands #3982, contract objects #3984) were published with no measurement of usefulness or calibration. This adds the measurement, in `pm-stack/aggregator`: - **Snapshot store** (`src/backtest.ts`): `createSnapshot` / `appendSnapshot` / `loadSnapshots` freeze weekly forecast captures as JSONL — model version, cutoff, source watermarks, and the full epic-completion contract objects (the minimal reproducible inputs: scope, input window/coverage, remaining units, reasons). One snapshot carries exactly one model version; mixed versions and non-epic contracts are refused at capture. - **Rolling-origin evaluation**: an evaluation as of T reads snapshots only — it sees no snapshot captured after T and no outcome recorded after T, so a backtest cannot leak the future into a forecast's score. Scores are per model version, never mixed. - **Calibration report**: sample counts, median absolute ETA error, and P80 interval coverage by 2/4/8-week horizon and confidence grade, compared against the documented no-change baseline (the subject's previous snapshot p50). The not-yet-calibrated gate is enforced: no `calibrated` state before 30 resolved forecasts across 8 distinct cutoffs; P80 coverage outside 70–90% in two successive eligible windows, or a model persistently worse than baseline, flags the report and sets `recommendUnavailable` (the documented disable/revert-to-unavailable rule). - **Quota-wall classification** is explicitly `not_evaluated`: the #3983 outcome history does not exist yet and the issue scope excludes it until it does. No forecast-derivation semantics change. - **Commands**: `scripts/forecast-snapshot.ts` (the weekly capture job) and `scripts/backtest-report.ts` (evaluate a store + outcome history, print the report). ## Tests - `bun test test/backtest.test.ts` — 9/9 pass: store round-trip + capture refusals, median-error/P80 metrics by horizon and grade, cutoff isolation (future-captured snapshot and late-recorded outcome are invisible), model-version separation, baseline scoring, and the calibration gate (calibrated / flagged / not-yet). - CLI smoke: snapshot script captured a fixture forecast; report script resolved it (median error 2d, coverage 1.0). - Neighboring suites `forecast-3982` + `forecast-contract-3984`: 48 pass, 1 fail — the failure is a 5s timeout in `deriveEpicEta > partially censored distribution (#6386)` that reproduces identically on clean main in the primary clone (pre-existing, untouched by this change). - `bunx tsc --noEmit`: 24 errors, the same 24 as clean main; none in the new files. Queue: task 14816, lane code-e. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: fix(pm-aggregator): /program compact pool rows + /quota analytics aggregates cache (#5082)
items.body: Fixes both live defects tracked on #5082 (PM broker surfaces), measured by the pool-quota steward on 2026-11-13. ## 1. /program HTML regrowth — 4,077,305 B and climbing daily **Root cause (measured, not guessed).** The pool section rendered every one of the 1,422 Project #4 pool items as a full interactive card (~2,791 B median): title/badges/links ~0.65 KB + status-request actbox **1,702,156 B total** + derived brief panel **1,347,229 B total**. The pool only ever grows — the orchestrator adds every filed item and nothing ever leaves — and 725 of the 1,422 items are Done. Daily growth tracked the filing rate (~+24 KB/day at plateau, +140–190 KB on busy days). /api/program.json stayed 26 KB the whole time: the growth was all HTML card furniture, none of it data. A Done item's brief is formulaic ("Next: No action — this item is done") and its actbox is an action control for work that is finished. **Fix (render.ts, `projectsBodyHtml`).** Full cards now render only for active work (Project status In Progress / In Review) and for epics at any status — an epic's rollup/forecast/spend are its substance (#3984, #4824) and epics are few (40). Every other item renders as a compact row — title, status/area/horizon/kind/state badges, issue + Project-item links, updated date — the same compact shape the per-project pages already use. The ⚠ disagreement badge still renders on compact rows, so no signal is lost. Counts, area chips, weights, the area filter and saved views all operate on the whole pool exactly as before; the JSON twins are untouched. Pool-section body, same live pool, old vs new code: **4,112,551 B → 1,067,703 B**. Full cards for active items are byte-identical to before (verified modulo the per-render form token). Page growth is now bounded by the active pool, not by cumulative history. **Tradeoff, stated plainly:** a Todo/Done non-epic item no longer carries its brief panel or status-request form on /program (both remain on its full surfaces — board/item views and GitHub). One test fixture follows the new contract: the #1279 forwarded-brief test in curation-1497.test.ts now uses an In Progress fixture, since briefs render on full cards; its with/without forwarding assertions are unchanged. ## 2. /quota slow — 5–19 s per load **Root cause (measured in-process against the live 21.7 GB OpenCode ledger, 656k route_attempt rows).** `buildQuotaAnalytics` ran seven route_attempt aggregate scans per build; only the two burn scans were cached (120 s). The other five — last-hour burn, credential coverage, hourly-7d, **day-of-week over the entire table (no WHERE)**, daily-21d — ran on **every** request: ~5.4 s of scans per warm build, ~10 s cold, all synchronous on Bun's single event loop, so concurrent page loads queued behind each other's scans (hence /quota at 9.4 s / 18.8 s and knock-on stalls on / and /today). Baseline in-process: cold 9,309 ms, warm ~5,100 ms. /api/quota.json was always fast (0.04 s) because it never builds analytics. **Fix (analytics-store.ts + server.ts).** All route_attempt aggregates now ride ONE stale-while-revalidate cache (5 min TTL, the loadActivity pattern this codebase already uses for its other slow scan): a fresh copy is served directly; a stale copy is served immediately while a background refresh recomputes one query per macrotask, so a refresh never monopolizes the loop. The first build in a process computes synchronously, and server.ts now pays that once at boot with a warm-up call, off the request path. The SQL is byte-for-byte the same queries, regrouped behind query helpers. **Equivalence:** old vs new builder output on identical inputs differs only by 4 route attempts that landed in the ~50 s between the two runs (attemptsTo and the counts containing them); every projection, window, unlock picture and WoW delta is identical. Warm build: **~5,100 ms → ~2 ms**; a stale-read build returns in ~2 ms with the previous aggregates. ## Verification (laptop, worktree) - `bunx tsc --noEmit`: error set identical to pristine main (zero new; none in src/). - `bun test` (full aggregator suite, 192 files): named-failure set identical to the pristine-main baseline (the live-source #1138/#1139/#1140 trio, the #1195 boot test, and load-sensitive hook timeouts fail on main too). The four suites covering pool cards (epics, forecast #3984, spend #4824, curation #1497) pass 35/35. - Live before/after numbers are posted on #5082 after deploy. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Project pool items that aren’t in progress or review, and aren’t epics, now appear as compact cards with key status and issue details. Active work and epics retain their full cards. * **Improvements** * Analytics views can reuse recent results and continue showing cached data while updates refresh. * Quota analytics now load at startup when possible, with a later retry if loading fails.

items.title: feat(pm-stack): flow analytics computation + JSON twin (#4829)
items.body: ## What Step 2 of the #1281 split (task 6953): flow analytics for the pm-stack aggregator, computed from the #3981 item-history store and exposed machine-first as the JSON twin the step-3 charts (#4830) will render. - **New pure module `src/flow-analytics.ts`** — `computeFlowAnalytics(cutoffs)` over `ItemHistoryCutoff[]` (the #3981 seam; no new store, no collector): - *Time-in-status* per item, aggregated per group. An interval between consecutive stored cutoffs accrues to the status observed at its start, and only when **both** bounding cutoffs are complete and available — the `weeklyTransitions` chain rule. - *Weekly throughput* per group, reusing `weeklyTransitions` so the week definition is identical to the forecasting series: issues only (design SS1), zero-completion weeks preserved as real observations. - *Grouping* follows the forecast subject model: `parentRef` (direct) else `epicRef` (ancestor) else the explicit unassigned group (`groupRef: null`); membership is read at each interval's start. - Every result carries the **computation window** (`fromCutoff`/`toCutoff`/counts) and a **gaps list** naming each incomplete or unavailable cutoff — gappy history degrades visibly, never silently, and gap-spanning intervals are attributed to no status and no week. - **`GET /api/flow-analytics.json`** in `server.ts`, beside `/api/forecasts.json`, reading the same `ItemHistoryStore`. ## Tests `test/flow-analytics-4829.test.ts` — fixture cutoffs covering: a complete window (per-epic time-in-status totals, per-item rows, throughput with a preserved zero week), a gappy window (incomplete cutoff breaks the chain, gap flagged, nothing zero-filled), an unavailable cutoff (gap; items seen only there create no group), a zero-completion week under complete coverage, the issues-only throughput unit (a merging PR accrues time-in-status but never counts as a completion), unset-status labelling, and empty history. Local verification (laptop, this branch): - `bun test test/flow-analytics-4829.test.ts` — **6 pass**. - Neighbouring suites (`item-history`, `forecast-3982`, `forecast-contract-3984`): 61 pass, 1 fail — `deriveEpicEta > partially censored distribution (#6386)` times out after 5000 ms. **Pre-existing**: the identical failure reproduces on a pristine worktree at current main, and `bunx tsc --noEmit` reports the identical 24 errors (all in `src/render.ts` / `test/aa-batches.test.ts`) on both trees; no errors in the files this PR touches. Fixes #4829. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: docs: design pm-stack forecasting (#1256)
items.body: ## Summary ```text current inputs (quota / pool / graph) + new item-history prerequisite ├─ ETA distribution (P50/P80 + sample confidence) ├─ quota exhaustion interval (reuses #3933 data/rules) └─ explainable stall score └─ shared forecast contract → Roadmap + Projects └─ rolling-origin backtests ``` Adds a dated forecasting design note and indexes it in `doc/README.md`. It answers all five questions in #1256, names the owner decisions, cites current source lines, and records that coverage is not item history, graph.ts does not carry blocked age, and the live quota data gap remains tracked by #3933. Implementation issues: #3981, #3982, #3983, #3984, #3986. GitHub reports #1184 already has 100 direct sub-issues and rejects additional direct links with HTTP 422. To preserve existing relations, these are native sub-issues of #1256, which is itself a native child of #1184; this hierarchy limitation is documented in the note and each issue. ## Evidence - **Before:** no forecasting design note; current inputs do not provide item-level completion/blocked-age history, and live quota ingestion/rate history is incomplete. - **After:** source-grounded design note with explicit 4-/8-week windows, sparse-sample handling, P50/P80 ranges, quota-wall inputs, stall-risk rules, presentation contract, and backtest/retirement criteria. - `git diff --check HEAD^ HEAD` — pass. - Relative Markdown links and source line anchors in the new note — pass. - Runtime tests — not applicable (documentation-only change). ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way Documentation and issue planning only; no runtime behavior changes. **Blast Radius:** low --- Need help on this PR?
